+    Decidable (IsIsolating G S) := by unfold IsIsolating; infer_instance

# Co-citation complexes and the limits of polynomial Betti growth

complex from the flag complex of its pairwise co-citation graph.

The principal structural result is a conformality criterion: the co-citation complex
coincides with the clique complex exactly when every graph clique is contained in a
single corpus entry.  The counting results then give a universal binomial ceiling on
all chain dimensions and hence on every Betti number arising from boundary ranks.
In particular, an `n`-vertex corpus has no homology in dimensions `n` and above, which
rules out an unqualified law of the form `β_k ≈ n^(k+1)` across all dimensions.

Hypothesis (Hypothesizer), ranked by expected impact: (1) a temporally filtered
co-citation hypergraph has phase transitions detectable by persistent `H₂`; (2) under a

conformality law; (4) corpus growth induces a monotone simplicial filtration; (5) every
`k`-th Betti number obeys the sharp binomial chain ceiling; and (6) unrestricted

open Classical Finset

namespace TheoremNetworkTopology

variable {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]

/-- A finite co-citation corpus: each member is the set of theorems cited by one item. -/
abbrev Corpus (V : Type*) := Finset (Finset V)

/-- The downward-closed co-citation complex generated by a corpus. -/
def coCitationComplex (C : Corpus V) : Finset (Finset V) :=
  Finset.univ.powerset.filter fun S => ∃ W ∈ C, S ⊆ W

/-
A face of the generated complex remains a face after deleting vertices.
-/
theorem coCitationComplex_downward (C : Corpus V) {S T : Finset V}
    (hS : S ∈ coCitationComplex C) (hTS : T ⊆ S) : T ∈ coCitationComplex C := by
  grind +locals

/-
Adding documents to a corpus can only add faces.
-/
theorem coCitationComplex_mono {C D : Corpus V} (hCD : C ⊆ D) :
    coCitationComplex C ⊆ coCitationComplex D := by
  intro S hS; simp_all +decide [ coCitationComplex ] ;
  exact ⟨ hS.choose, hCD hS.choose_spec.1, hS.choose_spec.2 ⟩

/-- The pairwise co-citation graph, also called the two-section of the corpus. -/
def coCitationGraph (C : Corpus V) : SimpleGraph V where
  Adj x y := x ≠ y ∧ ∃ W ∈ C, x ∈ W ∧ y ∈ W
  symm := by rintro x y ⟨hxy, W, hW, hx, hy⟩; exact ⟨hxy.symm, W, hW, hy, hx⟩
  loopless := ⟨fun x h => h.1 rfl⟩

/-
Every genuine co-citation face is a clique in the pairwise graph.
-/
theorem coCitationComplex_subset_cliqueFamily (C : Corpus V) :
    coCitationComplex C ⊆
      VRCliqueExtremalDeepening.cliqueFamily (coCitationGraph C) := by
  intro S hS
  obtain ⟨W, hW, hSW⟩ := (Finset.mem_filter.mp hS).right
  simp [VRCliqueExtremalDeepening.cliqueFamily, coCitationGraph];
  exact fun x hx y hy hxy => ⟨ hxy, W, hW, hSW hx, hSW hy ⟩

/-- `Conformal C` says that every pairwise clique has one common witnessing document. -/
def Conformal (C : Corpus V) : Prop :=
  ∀ S : Finset V, (coCitationGraph C).IsClique (↑S : Set V) → ∃ W ∈ C, S ⊆ W

/-
**Conformality criterion.** Pairwise data reconstructs the full co-citation complex
exactly when every graph clique has a common corpus witness.
-/
theorem coCitationComplex_eq_cliqueFamily_iff (C : Corpus V) :
    coCitationComplex C =
        VRCliqueExtremalDeepening.cliqueFamily (coCitationGraph C) ↔
      Conformal C := by
  constructor;
  · intro h S hS;
    replace h := Finset.ext_iff.mp h S; simp_all +decide [ coCitationComplex, VRCliqueExtremalDeepening.cliqueFamily ] ;
  · intro h_conformal
    ext S
    simp [coCitationComplex, VRCliqueExtremalDeepening.cliqueFamily, coCitationGraph];
    exact ⟨ fun ⟨ W, hW, hWS ⟩ => fun x hx y hy hxy => ⟨ hxy, W, hW, hWS hx, hWS hy ⟩, fun h => h_conformal S h ⟩

/-- Faces containing exactly `q` vertices. -/
def facesOfCard (C : Corpus V) (q : ℕ) : Finset (Finset V) :=
  (coCitationComplex C).filter fun S => S.card = q

/-
Every `q`-face is among the `q`-subsets of the ambient theorem set.
-/
theorem card_facesOfCard_le_choose (C : Corpus V) (q : ℕ) :
    (facesOfCard C q).card ≤ (Fintype.card V).choose q := by
  convert Finset.card_le_card _;
  any_goals exact Finset.powersetCard q Finset.univ;
  · rw [ Finset.card_powersetCard, Finset.card_univ ];
  · exact fun S hS => Finset.mem_powersetCard.mpr ⟨ Finset.subset_univ _, by simpa using Finset.mem_filter.mp hS |>.2 ⟩

/-- A rank-only presentation of a Betti number: chain dimension minus the ranks of the
incoming and outgoing boundary maps.  The side condition is the usual rank inequality. -/
def bettiFromRanks (C : Corpus V) (boundaryRank : ℕ → ℕ) (k : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  (facesOfCard C (k + 1)).card - (boundaryRank k + boundaryRank (k + 1))

/-
Boundary maps can only decrease homology dimension, giving the binomial ceiling.
-/
theorem bettiFromRanks_le_choose (C : Corpus V) (boundaryRank : ℕ → ℕ) (k : ℕ) :
    bettiFromRanks C boundaryRank k ≤ (Fintype.card V).choose (k + 1) := by
  exact le_trans ( Nat.sub_le _ _ ) ( card_facesOfCard_le_choose _ _ )

/-
Consequently every rank-presented Betti number has the coarser polynomial ceiling
`n^(k+1)`.  This is an upper bound, not an asymptotic equivalence.
-/
theorem bettiFromRanks_le_power (C : Corpus V) (boundaryRank : ℕ → ℕ) (k : ℕ) :
    bettiFromRanks C boundaryRank k ≤ (Fintype.card V) ^ (k + 1) := by
  exact le_trans ( bettiFromRanks_le_choose C boundaryRank k ) ( Nat.choose_le_pow _ _ )

/-
No face can have more vertices than the ambient theorem set.
-/
theorem facesOfCard_eq_empty_of_card_lt (C : Corpus V) {q : ℕ}
    (h : Fintype.card V < q) : facesOfCard C q = ∅ := by
  exact Finset.eq_empty_iff_forall_notMem.mpr fun x hx => not_lt_of_ge ( Finset.card_le_univ _ ) ( lt_of_lt_of_le h <| Finset.mem_filter.mp hx |>.2.symm ▸ Finset.card_le_card ( Finset.subset_univ _ ) )

**Dimension obstruction.** On `n` vertices, all rank-presented Betti numbers in
homological dimensions `k ≥ n` vanish, regardless of the citation pattern.
-/
theorem bettiFromRanks_eq_zero_of_card_le (C : Corpus V) (boundaryRank : ℕ → ℕ)

  unfold bettiFromRanks;
  rw [ facesOfCard_eq_empty_of_card_lt ];
  · norm_num;
  · linarith

**No uniform positive power law across dimensions.** For a nonempty theorem set,
the power `n^(k+1)` is positive while every rank-presented Betti number vanishes once

-/
theorem bettiFromRanks_ne_power_of_card_le [Nonempty V]
    (C : Corpus V) (boundaryRank : ℕ → ℕ) {k : ℕ} (h : Fintype.card V ≤ k) :
    bettiFromRanks C boundaryRank k ≠ (Fintype.card V) ^ (k + 1) := by
  rw [ bettiFromRanks_eq_zero_of_card_le C boundaryRank h ];
  exact ne_of_lt ( pow_pos ( Fintype.card_pos ) _ )

Corpus growth indexed by a filtration parameter induces a nested simplicial
filtration.
-/
theorem filtered_coCitationComplex_mono {ι : Type*} [Preorder ι]
    (C : ι → Corpus V) (hC : Monotone C) :
    Monotone (fun t => coCitationComplex (C t)) := by
  exact fun s t hst => coCitationComplex_mono ( hC hst )

A single document citing every theorem generates the full simplex.
-/
theorem coCitationComplex_singleton_univ :
    coCitationComplex ({Finset.univ} : Corpus V) = Finset.univ.powerset := by
  ext S; simp [coCitationComplex]

/-
The pairwise graph of that complete corpus is the complete graph.
-/
theorem coCitationGraph_singleton_univ :
    coCitationGraph ({Finset.univ} : Corpus V) = ⊤ := by
  ext x y; by_cases hxy : x = y <;> simp +decide [ hxy, coCitationGraph ] ;

The complete corpus is conformal, so its higher-order and flag constructions agree.

# Computational Evidence

## Small-case calculations

The three-theorem corpus

| document | cited theorems |
|---|---|
| A | `{0,1}` |
| B | `{0,2}` |
| C | `{1,2}` |

has all three pairwise co-citation edges. Its pairwise graph is therefore the complete graph on three vertices, whose clique complex contains the triangle `{0,1,2}`. The corpus complex itself contains only the empty face, three vertices, and three edges: no document witnesses the triple. Thus pairwise projection introduces one spurious two-simplex.

For a corpus on `n` theorems, direct enumeration gives the following universal ceilings for the number of potential `k`-simplices:

| `n` | vertices | edges | triangles | tetrahedra |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 2 | 2 | 1 | 0 | 0 |
| 3 | 3 | 3 | 1 | 0 |
| 4 | 4 | 6 | 4 | 1 |
| 5 | 5 | 10 | 10 | 5 |
| 6 | 6 | 15 | 20 | 15 |

These are the binomial coefficients `n choose (k+1)`. Since homology is a quotient of a subspace of the corresponding chain space, every Betti number is bounded by the entry in the relevant column.

## Counterexample hunt

The universal claim `β_k ≈ n^(k+1)` fails without additional quantifiers and a corpus model.

* If `k ≥ n`, there are no `(k+1)`-vertex faces, so `β_k = 0`, while `n^(k+1) > 0` for every nonempty corpus.
* A corpus consisting of one document containing every theorem generates a full simplex. It has the maximal possible face count but no positive-dimensional homology, showing that simplex abundance alone does not force large Betti numbers.
* The three-theorem example above shows that replacing genuine multiway co-citation by pairwise clique completion can change higher-dimensional topology.

The accompanying results establish these obstructions symbolically for every finite theorem type; the table is illustrative rather than the basis of the conclusions.

## Sequence search

The face ceilings are the rows of Pascal's triangle. No separate sequence identification is needed: the exact formula is the standard binomial coefficient `n choose (k+1)`.

## Interpretation boundary

No calculation on an unlabeled incidence complex can by itself establish that a first-homology class is a “school of mathematics” or that a second-homology class is a “paradigm shift.” Those are hypotheses relating topology to external semantic or temporal labels and require a labeled data set and a statistical validation protocol.

# Future Directions: Topology of Theorem Networks

## 1. A null model for higher-dimensional citation topology

**Conjecture.** In a sparse random corpus with bounded expected document size and theorem degrees converging to a nondegenerate distribution, each fixed-dimensional normalized Betti number has a deterministic limit, while the unnormalized Betti number is bounded above by the corresponding binomial face count and is typically of strictly smaller order.

The key insight is that the universal binomial ceiling controls the available chain generators, but boundary ranks—not simplex counts alone—determine the surviving topology.

**Why now?** The structural ceiling and dimension-vanishing theorem identify exactly which asymptotic claims are possible; specifying a random incidence model is the missing ingredient needed to replace an unsupported power law by a falsifiable limit theorem.

## 2. Conformality thresholds in temporal co-citation hypergraphs

**Conjecture.** For a growing random co-citation corpus, there is a sharp threshold at which every clique in the pairwise co-citation graph acquires a common document witness, and hence the higher-order corpus complex becomes equal to its flag completion.

The key insight is that equality of the two complexes is governed by one exact obstruction: pairwise compatibility without a global witness.

**Why now?** The three-theorem boundary example isolates the smallest obstruction, while the conformality criterion turns the disappearance of all such obstructions into a precise event whose threshold can be studied probabilistically.

## 3. Stability of semantic labels under topological perturbation

**Conjecture.** If research-community labels are defined independently of the citation complex, then no uniformly stable rule can recover them from first homology alone; recovery becomes possible only after adding vertex metadata or a generative assortativity assumption.

The key insight is that a cycle is an incidence pattern rather than a semantic object, so identical complexes can support incompatible assignments of mathematical schools.

**Why now?** Structural topology can now be cleanly separated from interpretation. This makes it possible to state identifiability assumptions explicitly and test whether metadata genuinely contributes information beyond graph connectivity.

## 4. Persistent detection of localized structural change

**Conjecture.** In a temporal corpus filtration with bounded document size, an abrupt increase followed by decay in persistent second homology detects a sustained failure of local conformality more reliably than raw triangle or tetrahedron counts.

The key insight is that pairwise projection can fill a spurious triangle even when no triple witness exists, whereas persistence across the genuine hypergraph filtration records whether the resulting cavity survives subsequent documents.

**Why now?** Monotonicity of the corpus complex provides a valid filtration, and the explicit strict-loss example supplies the elementary mechanism from which a statistical change-point theory can be built.

## 5. Extremal Betti profiles under document-size constraints

**Conjecture.** Among corpora on `n` theorems whose documents have size at most `d`, the maximum possible `k`-th Betti number is attained by a highly symmetric design and has order `n^(k+1)` only for fixed `k < d`, with constants depending essentially on both `d` and the coefficient field.

The key insight is that polynomial growth can be plausible in fixed dimension even though it is impossible uniformly across dimensions; document-size bounds determine which chain groups can exist at all.

**Why now?** The binomial ceiling supplies the correct ambient scale, while dimension vanishing rules out overgeneralization. The remaining extremal problem is concrete, finite, and testable on designs, multipartite constructions, and random bounded hypergraphs.

## Results established

The finite Hamming Library of length `L` over `A` symbols has exactly `A^L` points and is homeomorphic to `Fin (A^L)` with its discrete topology. # Computational Evidence

## Small cases

For an alphabet of size `A` and length `L`, direct enumeration predicts `A^L` books:

| `A` | `L` | number of books |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 2 | 1 | 2 |
| 2 | 2 | 4 |
| 2 | 3 | 8 |
| 3 | 2 | 9 |
| 4 | 3 | 64 |

For binary length `L = 4`, a decoder with only `2^(4-2) = 4` descriptions can name at most 4 of the 16 books, leaving at least 12 incompressible. The proved factorization gives `12 = (2^2 - 1) * 2^(4-2)`.

For binary length `L = 8`, the guaranteed numbers missed by decoders with deficiency `c` are:

| `c` | descriptions `2^(L-c)` | all books | guaranteed missed |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 128 | 256 | 128 |
| 2 | 64 | 256 | 192 |
| 3 | 32 | 256 | 224 |
| 4 | 16 | 256 | 240 |

## OEIS

For fixed alphabet size `A`, the library sizes as `L` varies are the geometric sequence `A^L`. For `A = 2` these are the powers of two (OEIS A000079): `1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, ...`.

## Counterexample hunt

The universal connectedness claim fails already at `A = 2`, `L = 1`: the books `0` and `1` are distinct isolated points. More generally, whenever `2 ≤ A` and `0 < L`, the all-zero and all-one books are explicit distinct isolated points. This counterexample pattern is formalized for all such `A` and `L` in `BorgesLibrary.hamming_not_connected`.

The apparent contradiction comes from confusing two structures. The Hamming *graph* can be path-connected by single-character edits, but the finite metric topology is discrete and therefore not topologically connected when it has more than one point.

# Future Directions

## Results established

The finite Hamming Library of length `L` over `A` symbols has exactly `A^L` points and is homeomorphic to `Fin (A^L)` with its discrete topology. Singleton books form a clopen basis, so this gives the standard dimension-zero certificate for a finite metrizable space, and the Library is totally disconnected.

The proposed simultaneous connectedness claim is false in every genuine case: if `2 ≤ A` and `0 < L`, two explicit constant books are distinct and the Library is not connected. Moreover, every continuous decoder from a preconnected parameter space into the Library is constant, so no such decoder can be surjective onto a nontrivial Library.

For any decoder with `N` programs, at most `N` books are generated and at least `A^L - N` are incompressible relative to that decoder. In the binary case, allowing `2^(L-c)` descriptions leaves at least `2^L - 2^(L-c)` books undescribed. This is the precise finite counting content of “almost all books are incompressible.” Kolmogorov complexity is decoder-dependent, so there is no machine-independent exact complexity assigned to an individual random book.

## Further formalization

1. Define prefix-free machines and prefix Kolmogorov complexity, then derive the same counting bound from Kraft's inequality for all programs shorter than a threshold.
2. Put the uniform probability measure on the finite Library and restate the cardinal bound as a probability estimate: the compressible fraction is at most `2^{-c}`.
3. Formalize Lebesgue covering dimension itself and connect the proved clopen-basis certificate to a theorem `coveringDimension = 0`; the current development proves the standard finite metrizable certificate rather than introducing a separate dimension theory.
4. Classify all degenerate connected cases (`L = 0`, or a one-symbol alphabet) and handle the empty-library corner case (`A = 0 < L`) explicitly.
5. Extend fixed-length libraries to infinite streams. Product spaces over finite discrete alphabets are Cantor-like: unlike the finite Library, they are compact and perfect while remaining totally disconnected.
6. Compare Hamming topology with graph connectivity of the Hamming graph. The graph is connected when single-symbol edits are allowed, while its metric topology is discrete; distinguishing these notions explains the original contradictory framing.
